title: New project
description: A small starting point: sets of items that contain every item below a picked one (n solutions). Replace the fragments with your own problem.

fragments.name: shared
fragments.text:
% Rules every solver needs: domains, constants, common definitions.
item(1..n).

fragments.name: abstraction
fragments.text:
% Proposes candidates. Every solution must be a candidate; the check removes the rest.
% Here: any non-empty set of items.
1 { pick(I) : item(I) }.
#show pick/1.

fragments.name: glue
fragments.text:
% The atoms the abstraction and the check share: glue(T) makes T an interface atom.
glue(pick(I)) :- item(I).

fragments.name: check
fragments.text:
% Looks for a counterexample to the candidate; the interface atoms (pick/1) are fixed.
% Here: a candidate is wrong if it picks an item but not a smaller one.
{ gap(I,J) : item(I), item(J), I < J } = 1.
:- gap(I,J), pick(I).
:- gap(I,J), not pick(J).
% relevant(T): the interface atoms the counterexample depends on. The refinement says
% that one of them must change.
relevant(pick(I)) :- gap(I,J).
relevant(pick(J)) :- gap(I,J).

loop.text:
solver A = shared + abstraction
solver C = shared + check          options "--heuristic=Domain"
link   G = A -> C via shared + glue

search A:
    on candidate M:
        X = C.solve(assume G(M))
        if X:
            reject M with G.clause(M, X)
